newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says hopes scheme on Nissan Life ready in June.
newsitem.headline: MOF says hopes scheme on Nissan Life ready in June.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) hopes the general policy on a scheme for Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co will be drawn up during June, a senior MOF official said on Tuesday.

Asked by a parliamentary committee when a plan to wind up the failed insurance company will be drawn up, the official said, "It would be good if a general direction can be hammered out during June or sooner."
He said that the scheme needed to be drawn up as soon as possible, as Nissan Life's policyholders are becoming worried.

He also said that insurance firms are likely to hold their annual conventions towards the summer and that any decisions, such as a transfer of contracts, would need policyholders' approval at that time.
Nissan Mutual, a medium-sized Tokyo-based life insurer, was ordered by MOF to halt most of its business on April 25.

The company has said it expects to report a net loss of 52.5 billion yen for the business year that ended in March, as a result of heavy losses through excessive stock and real estate investments during Japan's late-1980s "bubble" era of inflated asset prices. MOF has said that the failure was due to poor management of its investment portfolio.
The Life Insurance Association of Japan, an industry body representing life insurers, said it would work out a liquidation scheme for Nissan Life.
